Subject: Re: Discovery — Private deployment clarifications

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. A quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can align with our security and infra teams: 

Summary of our needs (from the call):
- Data residency: PHI must remain within our AWS accounts in us-west-2.
- Network: Air-gapped-like controls preferred — no public ingress to model serving nodes; outbound egress highly restricted.
- Key management: Customer-managed keys (KMS) mandatory.
- Audit requirements: Detailed token/user-level audit logs for 1 year.

Questions:
1) Do you support a Private deployment with a VPC-only control plane and strictly private egress?
2) Any existing customers running with an air-gap/very restrictive egress posture?
3) What artifacts can you share for our security review (SOC2, architecture diagram, network flow example)?

I've attached the network diagram we sketched during the call and our high-level HIPAA checklist. Looking to consolidate answers to share with infra/security by end of day Friday.

Thanks,
Alice
VP Product, HealthCorp

Attachments: healthcorp-network-diagram.png, HIPAA_Security-Checklist.pdf

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery — Private deployment clarifications

Hi Alice — great talking earlier, and thanks for the diagram and checklist. Below is a concise post-call recap + proposed next steps so your infra/security teams have something concrete to review.

Recap of pain & goals (as I heard them):
- Pain: current hosted LLM vendors either require public egress for model updates or do not provide customer-managed KMS and fine-grained audit logs — creates compliance risk for PHI workloads.
- Goal: Private/VPC deployment that keeps all inference traffic inside HealthCorp accounts (no public ingress), supports CMK (AWS KMS), and provides 12+ months of detailed audit logs.

What Redwood can offer (summary):
- Private deployment (VPC mode) installed into a customer-managed AWS account in us-west-2.
- Control plane options: private control plane over a secure peering/VPN link or a fully air-gapped on-prem package (we have an air-gap playbook).
- Networking: our serving nodes can be deployed in private subnets with no public IPs; we support strict egress controls and can run model downloads via an out-of-band transfer process controlled by your infra team.
- KMS/Keys: support for customer-managed AWS KMS keys + HSM integrations where required.
- Audit & logging: token-level request logs, model-version metadata, and operator actions — configurable retention (we can ship logs to your S3 or a Splunk/Datadog endpoint).

Attachments I’ll share for security review (attached to this thread):
- Redwood_Private_VPC_Architecture.pdf (includes network flow and peering options)
- SOC2-Type2-Report-Summary.pdf
- Airgap_Installation_Playbook.pdf

Open items / next steps:
1) Camila to share the three artifacts above with HealthCorp security by EOD. 
2) Alice to confirm whether infra prefers private control plane (peering/VPN) vs fully air-gapped install.
3) If private control plane: schedule a short network-design sync with both infra teams + our solutions engineer (Rishi) — proposing Thu 07/01 10am PT.
4) Marissa (legal) will follow up on initial commercial/licensing constraints for on-prem and air-gap options.

Doable timeline: once we lock on control-plane model, solutions + infra can produce a minimal technical plan in ~2 business days and provide onboarding estimates.

Thanks — I’ll attach the artifacts and send to your security alias now.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

Hi Alice — looping in legal/enterprise for the licensing side. Quick notes from my side: 

- Commercial model: Private (VPC) deployments are typically contracted as a combined platform + support fee with an annual commitment. Air-gapped on-prem installs may require a separate services/installation SOW.
- Data handling: We can commit in the contract that HealthCorp is the data controller; Redwood will not store customer data outside your controlled S3 buckets when deployed in your account.
- Security artifacts: Camila will share SOC2 summary and architecture; we can provide the full SOC2 package under an NDA if needed.
- Next legal steps: If you want to proceed, I can send an initial SOW + MSA redline template for your counsel to review.

If infra/security confirm private control plane with peering, send over the CIDR blocks and preferred peering/VPN details and we’ll have Rishi and our infra team produce an MLP (minimal launch plan).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise GTM | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
